Metadata only: set categories (Development, Automation, Agents). No content change.

2.0.1: restores the optional caged worker (foreman-cworker.sh) removed in 2.0.0. Removing it did not remove the underlying risk — workers were simply unsandboxed instead — and cost users the more isolated option. Content is identical to 1.1.3: pinned worker image, validated mounts, dropped capabilities, read-only root filesystem, and a documented caveat that the container's network is not restricted.

2.0.0 (breaking): the optional Docker caged worker (foreman-cworker.sh) is removed. It gave a container an API key with unrestricted network egress, and closing that properly needs an allowlisting proxy this skill should not ship. Dispatch through handoff into per-task git worktrees is unchanged. The docs now state plainly that workers are not sandboxed — isolation is by git worktree plus the intake checks — and that a hard boundary means running the whole setup inside a VM or container you control.

1.1.3: declares its requirements in the frontmatter (binaries, config file, and every environment variable it reads, per the registry skill format); the CI gate template pins actions/checkout to a commit SHA with read-only permissions; the dispatch chapter now spells out what --force and other permission-skipping backends mean and why they must stay inside a task worktree. The caged worker still has unrestricted network access, as documented.

1.1.2: documentation correction. The caged worker's API endpoint is configuration, not a network boundary — the container's network is not restricted, so code inside it could use the key elsewhere. The docs now say this plainly and recommend a dedicated low-limit key, plus an allowlisting proxy if you need a hard boundary. No behaviour change.

1.1.1: pins the worker supply chain (handoff-cli==4.0.2, base image by digest, claude-code@2.1.270; the caged worker only runs an immutable sha256 image reference) and validates what the cage mounts: only a git-registered task worktree directly under FOREMAN_WORKTREE_ROOT (never $HOME, /, the main checkout or a symlink escape) and a regular prompt file inside the task directory. The container now runs with all capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges and a read-only root filesystem.

1.1.0: probes the worker pool before dispatch (backend-health.sh: login/quota/config/network failures are skipped with cooldowns and never counted as rework); every task gets its own git worktree (worktree-setup.sh, mandatory --cwd); intake now requires a real commit and checks the diff at commit level, closing a hole where an uncommitted delivery merged as a silent no-op; fleet-check probes the pool and warns on shared CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; the description now discloses probes, Docker, key passing and permission skipping up front.

Supersedes 1.0.4, which was published without its intended change. Documents the credential boundary of the caged worker inline: where DEEPSEEK_API_KEY comes from, that it is exposed only to the process inside the container, that it is never written to disk nor copied into the mounted worktree, that it authenticates against exactly one endpoint, and that it disappears when the container exits.

Documents the credential boundary of the caged worker inline: where DEEPSEEK_API_KEY comes from, that it is exposed only to the process inside the container, that it is never written to disk or copied into the mounted worktree, that it authenticates against exactly one endpoint, and that it disappears when the container exits.

Security hardening: removed a curl-pipe-to-bash hint, stopped echoing the value of ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (it can carry a token), replaced a stat of the codex credential file with 'codex login status', pinned the container base image and npm dependency, and dropped the keyword list from the description. Added a 'What this skill touches' trust-boundary section covering what it writes, reads, which credential the caged worker receives, and what it never transmits.

The registry does not carry Dockerfiles - not in a subdirectory and not flattened either - so the worker image is now built from a Dockerfile inlined in dispatch.md via heredoc, verified by running the documented command end to end.

Fix: subdirectories are dropped on install, so worker-container/Dockerfile moved to top-level worker.Dockerfile and all references updated. Scripts are documented with 'bash <file>' since the executable bit does not survive install. Corrected the description of what 'handoff new' prints.
Initial release. Dispatch chapter runs on the public handoff CLI as-is; the dynamic acceptance step is tool-agnostic via FOREMAN_HARDENING_CMD.
